long_biography.plain_text:
Joining Putnam Lovell after selling his boutique in 1997 placed Roberto de Guardiola inside a larger investment bank while preserving his specialism in the investment-management industry. He advised on transactions between fund managers and strategic buyers, then returned to lead a firm bearing his own name.

De Guardiola's method was built on persistent contact with closely held firms. He recalled sending hundreds of letters before market consolidation turned those approaches into regular calls from prospective sellers. His Wharton training and transaction experience also led to board roles, including Invesco and American Farmland Company, where he chaired audit and compensation committees.
